request.clinical_notes:
68-year-old male presenting with persistent right lower lobe pulmonary nodule. CT chest (01/15/2026) demonstrates a 1.8 cm spiculated nodule in the RLL, increased from 1.2 cm on prior CT (10/12/2025), consistent with interval growth over 3 months. PET/CT (01/22/2026) shows FDG avidity with SUV max of 4.2, concerning for malignancy.

PMH: COPD (mild, GOLD stage I), hypertension, hyperlipidemia. 40 pack-year smoking history, quit 5 years ago. No prior history of malignancy. Family history significant for lung cancer (father, age 72). Medications: albuterol inhaler PRN, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Physical exam: Vitals BP 132/78, HR 76, RR 16, SpO2 95% on room air. Lungs with decreased breath sounds at right base; no wheezing or crackles. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs (01/20/2026): WBC 9.2 K/uL, Hgb 14.1 g/dL, Platelets 245 K/uL, INR 1.0, Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, BUN 18 mg/dL. Comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits.

Pulmonary function tests (01/18/2026): FEV1 78% predicted, FVC 82% predicted, FEV1/FVC ratio 0.73, DLCO 71% predicted. Patient is an acceptable surgical candidate.

Patient completed a 14-day course of amoxicillin-clavulanate with no resolution of the nodule. Given the spiculated morphology, interval growth, FDG avidity (SUV 4.2), and significant smoking history, there is high suspicion for primary lung malignancy per Fleischner Society guidelines. Recommend CT-guided transbronchial lung biopsy (CPT 31628) for tissue diagnosis. Risks including pneumothorax and bleeding were discussed; patient consents to proceed.

request.clinical_notes:
REASON FOR REQUEST: Bronchoscopy with transbronchial lung biopsy, single lobe (CPT 31628), for tissue diagnosis of an enlarging, PET-avid right lower lobe pulmonary nodule suspicious for primary lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 70-year-old male, former smoker (45 pack-years, quit 2019), with a persistent dry cough for 4 months. Chest CT 07/10/2026 showed a 1.3 cm solid spiculated RLL nodule. Repeat CT 10/09/2026 shows growth to 1.9 cm (volume doubling time about 90 days). PET/CT 10/20/2026: nodule FDG-avid, SUV max 5.1; no nodal or distant uptake. Brock model malignancy risk 58%. Meets Fleischner Society and ACCP criteria for tissue sampling (solid nodule > 8 mm, growth, high pretest probability).

PRIOR TREATMENT: 10-day course of amoxicillin-clavulanate (07/2026) and 4 weeks of observation with no change in symptoms; interval growth on CT excludes an inflammatory process.

SEVERITY AND FUNCTION: Persistent cough disturbing sleep, 4 kg unintentional weight loss over 3 months, ECOG performance status 1.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Mild COPD (GOLD 1), hypertension, type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 6.8%). Medications: tiotropium, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID. No anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents. Allergies: none known.

PRE-PROCEDURE ASSESSMENT: PFTs 10/22/2026: FEV1 74% predicted, DLCO 69% predicted. Labs 10/22/2026: platelets 238 K/uL, INR 1.0, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. ASA class II; acceptable candidate for moderate sedation bronchoscopy.

PLAN AND RATIONALE: Case reviewed at the multidisciplinary thoracic tumor board 10/24/2026; consensus recommendation is bronchoscopic transbronchial biopsy for diagnosis before any surgical resection or stereotactic radiation. Bronchoscopic route preferred over CT-guided transthoracic biopsy because of emphysema near the pleura (higher pneumothorax risk). Result will determine treatment (lobectomy vs SBRT) and staging. Risks (pneumothorax, bleeding, infection) and alternatives discussed; written informed consent obtained 10/24/2026.

REASON FOR REQUEST: Endobronchial ultrasound with transbronchial needle aspiration of 1-2 mediastinal lymph node stations (CPT 31652) for diagnosis and staging of suspected non-small cell lung cancer.

HISTORY: 65-year-old female, former smoker (35 pack-years, quit 2021), with 3 months of cough and 3 kg weight loss. Chest CT 09/30/2026: 2.6 cm left upper lobe mass with enlarged subcarinal (station 7, 1.8 cm short axis) and right lower paratracheal (station 4R, 1.4 cm) lymph nodes. PET/CT 10/14/2026: LUL mass SUV max 9.2; stations 7 and 4R FDG-avid (SUV 6.1 and 4.8); no distant disease. Brain MRI 10/16/2026 negative.

GUIDELINE BASIS: NCCN and ACCP guidelines recommend invasive mediastinal staging, preferably EBUS-TBNA, for suspected lung cancer with enlarged or PET-positive mediastinal nodes, before any treatment decision. Sampling the nodes gives diagnosis and stage in one minimally invasive procedure; contralateral 4R involvement would make the disease N3 (stage IIIB) and change treatment from surgery to chemoradiation.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypothyroidism, osteoarthritis. Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg. Not on anticoagulants. Allergies: penicillin (rash).

PRE-PROCEDURE ASSESSMENT: PFTs 10/15/2026 FEV1 81% predicted. Labs 10/15/2026: platelets 265 K/uL, INR 1.0. ECOG 0. ASA II.

PLAN: Reviewed at multidisciplinary thoracic tumor board 10/17/2026; EBUS-TBNA of stations 7 and 4R recommended as the first diagnostic and staging step. Risks and alternatives (mediastinoscopy) discussed; informed consent obtained.
